_why: Every Faust claim the system prompt makes in PROSE, paired with what the
installed compiler actually does. tests/test_prompt_claims.py enforces both
directions: each entry here must still appear in the prompt, and each claim the
extractors find in the prompt must appear here. Neither file can drift alone.
This exists because on 2026-07-27 the prompt was found teaching `let`, a
construct Faust has never had, for weeks. --verify-prompt resolves ns.func
references and saw nothing wrong, because the claim was prose. Compiling the
few-shots saw nothing either, because the claim was not in a few-shot.
fails     `program` must NOT compile, and stderr must contain `expect_error`.
template  contains metavariables (A, B, E, N, MAX, ...) or an ellipsis, so it
cannot be compiled literally. Recorded so completeness stays honest
rather than quietly skipping what it cannot check.

definitions.note: The prompt's positive example for declaring an argument.
The prompt's counter-example: `never echoCh = x * 0.5;`. Today's stereo-delay failure was exactly this — the model copied the echoCh few-shot and dropped the parameter list.
P6 #2, ping-pong. A self-reference outside a delay is a compile-time cycle, not a delay line.
The prompt's with{} form, given verbatim. Was recommended but never demonstrated until f3453c4; P6 #10 was `unexpected WITH`.
L and R are metavariables named as such in the same sentence.
PF-024 syntax:FLOAT. The generated ping-pong wrote `wet.0*mix`; the 0 after the dot lexes as a FLOAT. Faust has no channel indexing.
PF-024 syntax:EXTRA. The generated sidechain compressor wrote a C-style ternary. select2 is the replacement, checked under expressions above.

error_claims.expect_error: must be equal to the number of inputs
error_claims.note: PARAPHRASE, not compiler output. Faust emits: 'The number of outputs [2] of A must be equal to the number of inputs [1] of lowpass(2)(800)'. The quoted form appears nowhere in stderr. Recorded rather than silently corrected because the prompt is Tier 2 and generate.py feeds real stderr back on retry, so the two wordings should probably converge. docs/BUGS.md uses the same paraphrase.

_why_expressions: Claims the prompt makes as bare EXPRESSIONS -- not definitions, and carrying no
quoted compiler error. test_prompt_claims.py's own 'NOT COVERED' note named this
as its blind spot, and the PF-024/PF-032 prompt edit (2026-07-29) walked straight
into it: it added select2's argument ORDER and the (_ , !) channel-selection
idiom, both of which are load-bearing and neither of which any test could see.
Order and side cannot be checked by compiling -- both orders compile. So each
entry names a constant that must SURVIVE and one that must NOT, and the test reads
the folded constant out of the generated C++. That checks the semantics the prompt
actually asserts, not merely that the syntax parses.

expressions.note: cond=0 must select the FIRST value argument. If Faust ever reversed this the prompt would be teaching the branches backwards, and every generated conditional would be inverted while compiling perfectly.
! is the cut primitive. Both (_ , !) and (! , _) compile and have the same arity, so only the value distinguishes them.
The mirror of the entry above; asserted separately so a change that broke one direction could not hide behind the other.
